title: Add KMS denylist integration and audit-consistency fence for tenant residency manifests
author: Sofia Nguyen
description:
Motivation: customers and internal controls have asked for a mechanism to block specific KMS key identifiers (denylist) at the service boundary while ensuring audit logs remain consistent for residency policy enforcement. This PR introduces a service-level KMS denylist (operator-provided) that short-circuits key usage and records a deterministic audit 'fence' event when requests are refused due to residency/KMS policy conflicts.

What this change does (high level):
- Adds a KMS denylist lookup and enforcement hook in the KMS allocator middleware. Operator-provided denylist entries are loaded from the residency manifest and cached with TTL and proof-of-origin metadata.
- When a denylist hit occurs, the request is rejected with 403 + structured error code (residency.kms_denylist) and an immutable audit fence event is emitted with fields: request_id, tenant_id, claimed_region, denied_key_id, policy_version, decision_time. The fence event is formatted for downstream audit collectors and is tagged to prevent accidental redaction.
- Introduces an audit-consistency middleware that correlates KMS decisions with residency manifests to detect drift between deployed denylist entries and the operator manifest (background reconciliation job + one-off check endpoint).
- Adds small operator UI telemetry hooks and a README describing how to update the residency manifest, contract tests for fence event shape, and a migration job for older audit consumers.

Why this is safe:
- Denylist enforcement is opt-in per-cluster via operator config; default behavior is unchanged.
- We use a fast in-memory cache with signed manifest checks to avoid per-request crypto; background reconciler validates signatures periodically.
- All audit fence events are written to the existing immutable audit pipeline; no new storage paths are introduced.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit tests for KMS allocator denylist path and fence event construction.
- Integration tests that exercise reject+audit behavior in the staging audit pipeline.
- Canary rollout: bind denylist enforcement to flag operator.kms_enforce_denylist with percentage-based rollout.
- Post-rollout checklist includes monitoring for an increase in residency.kms_denylist metrics and reconciliation alerts.

Related work: Linear ENG-4301 (residency policy hardening), ENG-4479 (audit pipeline schema v2), and doc ticket DOC-189 (operator habits).

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed by security and compliance
- [x] Unit/integration tests added
- [x] Backwards-compatible audit format with migration notes
- [x] Canaries and feature flag support

Notes for reviewers: look closely at KMS allocator change for contention and the audit fence schema; there is a small risk of double-emitting events if the allocator retry path is exercised — I added an idempotency token derived from request_id + decision_time to dedupe in the audit sink.

review_comments: Marco Li: Please check allocator hot path; are we doing a synchronous manifest verification on cold-start? That will spike latency.

Sofia Nguyen: Good point — manifest verification is async on startup; allocator consults cache only and triggers background verify. Updated both code paths and tests to cover that (see commit d4e5f6a).
Priya Patel: Audit fence schema looks fine but we need to ensure it is consistent with ENG-4479 schema v2. Can you add a compatibility shim?
Sofia Nguyen: Added a migration shim in fence_writer.go and documented the mapping in docs. Integration tests assert both formats.
James O'Connor: Approve after unit tests finish — particularly want assertions around idempotency tokens to avoid duplicate audit rows.
CI: unit tests failed on first run due to flaky reconciliation test; reworked test timing and re-run passed.
release_notes: Introduces operator-managed KMS denylist enforcement and emits deterministic 'residency.kms_denylist' audit fence events on denied requests. Backwards-compatible audit migration shim included. Feature is off by default and gated by operator.kms_enforce_denylist.
